restore_and_deletion_protocol: Root must read this complete whitelist and its required small primary evidence, and confirm the currently active input closures do not consume either target.
Root first publishes this whitelist alone as a normal commit; that publication is separate from any deletion.

Immediately before deletion, read fresh current tree metadata and require BOTH exact target paths to have their listed full40 Git blob and byte size. If either differs or is absent, stop this whitelist action.
Use one ordinary non-force Git change deleting only the two listed report paths, preserving every other remote path and all current mathematical/open obligations.
Do not rewrite history, truncate reports, change old manifests, alter sources, remove native/canonical files, rerun old successful calculations, or reclassify any incomplete result.

For future access, restore the complete immutable bytes by git show <restore_commit>:<same_path> into the exact original path in the authorized working tree; verify byte count, Git blob and SHA256 before use. No mathematical producer is a restoration mechanism.
On a non-fast-forward publication, retain the existing operational true-pull/README-review policy and rebuild against the new remote state. This whitelist does not relax it.
